data.title: Owlet withdraws 2026 outlook amid camera cable guard update with $13M-$18M net Q4 impact estimate
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Owlet (OWLT) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We made very strong progress in the quarter, delivering on our priority to drive profitable growth." (Co-Founder, President, CEO & Director Kurt Workman) "Third quarter 2026 revenue was $30.4 million" and "gross margin was 53.8%" with "operating income... positive $1.2 million" and "adjusted EBITDA... $3.5 million" plus "$2.2 million in operating cash flow." (CEO Workman)
  • "Owlet was made aware that a family in our community lost their child after their toddler reached an unsecured camera cable and became tangled in it." (CEO Workman) "This involves only the cable guard accessory that ships with our cameras. It does not involve the camera itself or our FDA-cleared Dream Sock." (CEO Workman)
  • "We have issued a formal stop-ship notice across our retail channels." (CEO Workman) "Retailers will stop selling the affected units, which are Dream Sight and Dream Duo" and "Dream Sock is not impacted at retail or any other channels." (CEO Workman)
  • "These unknowns create a range of fourth quarter outcomes that's too wide for us to guide responsibly. So we are withdrawing our 2026 outlook." (CEO Workman) "Apart from the effects of these actions, we were in a position to reaffirm our 2026 guidance." (CEO Workman)
  • "We estimate the expense for producing and shipping replacement cable guards, logistics, customer support, legal and consulting fees at approximately $7 million to $10 million" and "we estimate retailer returns of $9 million to $12 million, which will be recorded as a reduction of revenue in the fourth quarter." (Chief Financial Officer Amanda Crawford)

Outlook

  • "Due to the safety update, we are withdrawing our full year 2026 outlook, which was revenue of $118 million to $122 million, gross margin of 53% to 55% and adjusted EBITDA of $10.75 million to $12.75 million." (CFO Crawford)
  • "Three of them we can reasonably estimate today" including "the $9 million to $12 million in retailer returns," "the offset of $3 million to $4 million for returned inventory that can be reworked and resold in the future" and "$7 million to $10 million in direct program costs, which is a total net impact of $13 million to $18 million." (CFO Crawford)
  • "There are 3 impacts we can't yet fully quantify" including "the timing of retailer replenishment" with "approximately $2 million to $5 million of initial load-in revenue," "the potential impact on demand" during "Black Friday and holiday sales periods," and "any potential insurance recovery, which could be up to $10 million." (CFO Crawford)

Financial Results

  • "Q3 total revenue was $30.4 million, down 4.9% versus $32 million in the prior year." (CFO Crawford) "Subscription revenue grew to a record $3.6 million" and "subscription gross margin was 68.4%." (CFO Crawford)
  • "Cash and cash equivalents... were $31.6 million" and "combined with $7.9 million of availability under our Wells Fargo credit facility, total available liquidity was approximately $39.5 million to end Q3." (CFO Crawford)
  • "Amazon had removed all of them by the end of September. As a result, Owlet Dream Sock is now the only baby monitor on Amazon that tracks instant vital signs." (CFO Crawford)

Q&A

  • Owen Rickert, Northland Capital Markets: "is the safety issue specific solely to the camera line?" Kurt Workman: "the cable guard is an accessory that ships with all of our camera and Duo products... it doesn't impact Dream Sock sales, which is roughly 70% of the business." (President & CEO Workman)
  • Owen Rickert, Northland Capital Markets: "does the cable guard safety update change the rollout time line" for Owlet One? Kurt Workman: "this won't impact Owlet One time lines" and "that will likely begin to roll out in a more prominent way on our website over the coming months." (President & CEO Workman)
  • Benjamin Haynor, Lake Street Capital Markets: question on Owlet One economics; Amanda Crawford: "with the recurring membership that we've been testing at $19 a month, the breakeven... is right now just a few months." (CFO Crawford)
  • Benjamin Haynor, Lake Street Capital Markets: question on safety update outreach and channel exposure; Kurt Workman: "there is an in-app safety update" and "I believe there's about 40,000 units in the channel today between Cam and Duo." (President & CEO Workman)
  • Jungwon Kim, TD Cowen: question on brand impact and Amazon trends; Kurt Workman: "there may be some short-term headwinds" but "long term, I really believe that the company that does the most for its customers will continue to build trust with parents." (President & CEO Workman) Amanda Crawford: "Prime Big Deal Days... was actually up 48%" for Dream Sock. (CFO Crawford)
  • Steven Lichtman, William Blair: question on restarting camera manufacturing; Kurt Workman: "manufacturing is not on hold" and "there was a pause in sales with our retailers for the old cameras with the old cable guard units." (President & CEO Workman)
  • Steven Lichtman, William Blair: question on whether returns include Dream Sock; Amanda Crawford: "it includes the Dream Sight camera and the Dream Duo, which is the bundle sold with the Dream Sock and camera." (CFO Crawford)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, with questions centered on scope, brand fallout, channel inventory exposure, and operational timing, including "what are the factors that need to happen" to lift the hold (Steven Lichtman, William Blair) and whether there is "potential broader impact to the brand itself" (Jungwon Kim, TD Cowen).
  • Management: slightly positive in tone on fundamentals but defensive/clarifying on safety scope, using repeated precision such as "just to be clear" and "I want to reiterate the scope" while emphasizing action and uncertainty, including "withdrawing our full year 2026 outlook" due to a range "too wide... to guide responsibly." (President & CEO Workman; CFO Crawford)
  • Versus the prior quarter, management moved from "we are reaffirming our revenue outlook of $118 million to $122 million" (Chief Financial Officer Amanda Crawford, Q2) to "we are withdrawing our full year 2026 outlook" (CFO Crawford, Q3), and analyst tone shifted from growth mechanics (subscription, telehealth, Web Pay) to crisis handling and Q4 visibility.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance posture changed from "we are reaffirming our revenue outlook of $118 million to $122 million" (CFO Crawford, Q2) to "we are withdrawing our full year 2026 outlook" tied to the camera cable guard update. (CFO Crawford, Q3)
  • Strategic narrative broadened from subscription/Web Pay expansion in Q2 (including "rolling Web Pay out in Q3" (CEO Workman, Q2)) to Q3 being dominated by product safety actions, stop-ship/stop-sale, and estimated Q4 financial impacts; product expansion still continued with "the Owlet Smart Thermometer, which we launched this week" and additional AI/subscription feature road maps. (CEO Workman, Q3)
  • Analyst focus shifted from subscription attach/retention and telehealth integration in Q2 to safety scope, brand trust, retail inventory returns, and timing of replenishment in Q3.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Because the cable guard ships in the box with every camera and Dream Duo, this creates logistical and financial challenges in the fourth quarter" and "there may also be a potential impact on demand we can't yet predict." (President & CEO Workman)
  • "Any recovery is subject to the policy's terms, conditions and retention. We have not recognized any insurance recovery to date and the timing and amount of any recovery are uncertain." (CFO Crawford)
  • "We have reported to the appropriate regulatory agencies as is standard practice, and there may be additional steps we need to take." (President & CEO Workman)

Final Takeaway

Owlet’s management emphasized Q3 profitability milestones and accelerating subscription momentum while detailing a voluntary camera cable guard safety update that triggered a retail stop-ship/stop-sale on Dream Sight and Dream Duo, estimated Q4 costs and returns, and the withdrawal of the company’s full-year 2026 outlook due to demand and replenishment uncertainty; management repeatedly clarified that the issue is limited to the cable guard accessory and stated Dream Sock remains available across channels, including Black Friday.

data.title: Cresud expects a 'very good year' as planted area rises 3%
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Cresud (CRESY) Q1 2027

Management view

  • "We are beginning a very good campaign" and "we are growing like 3% in planted area, mainly in Argentina," said (Second Vice Chairman, CEO, & GM Alejandro Elsztain), adding that "the prospects are very good related to climatic things in Argentina mainly" because "El Niño is coming to the region" and "the one probably will be more benefit is the Humid Pampas area."
  • On near-term crop progress, (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) said "100% of the area was planted" for wheat, harvest has begun in the north, and "the conditions are very good" and "they are better than budget," while in Brazil "soybeans in mainly Mato Grosso area was 100% planted in very good conditions" but there are "some doubts about the climate affecting Bahia and Mapito region."
  • On livestock profitability, (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) said "stable prices" are "affecting some of the results of the cattle business" and "we are expecting a little lower margins comparing to last year," despite "very good quarters related to production."
  • On farmland monetization and capital returns, (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) said Cresud "sold 2,600 hectares" at Rio do Meio farm "for close to BRL 100 million in installments" ("represent close to BRL 79 million in current value"), and added: "IRSA paid to Cresud $75.6 million and Cresud distributed $75.5 million" with "70% in cash and 30% in-kind in IRSA shares, representing a dividend yield close to 9%."
  • On FyO and digital strategy, (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) said FyO closed the year "passing 8.3 million tons, highest of our history, making an EBITDA of $20 million" and highlighted an acquisition-driven shift: FyO invested "$550,000" in Agrofy as part of a "$1 million" round, and "is taking the majority stake" and "now is being the controlling shareholder" to make "synergies with the rest of the lines of business of FyO."
  • From IRSA consolidation, (Chief Financial & Administrative Officer Matias Gaivironsky) said IRSA "posted a loss" of "ARS 6.3 million, completely attributable to the fair value of the investment properties" and described operating trends: "the rental EBITDA, we saw a decrease of 2% in pesos terms" ("1% in shopping malls, 11% in offices and 6% in hotels"), while "in dollar terms, we will have around 20% increase compared with the previous year."

Outlook

  • (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) tied near-term performance to weather and early planting cadence: "this year was a lot about the rain and the climate conditions" and "the thing finally are positive for our plantations," while noting Brazil’s "uneven rainfall distribution during Niño" and that "the drought could be coming to northern parts" affecting "Western Bahia and Mapito regions" but "very positive in Mato Grosso area."
  • (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) framed expected profitability improvement in row crops as early-stage: "Prices for the next campaign are better to last year" and "we are expecting an improving in quantity and in margins in soybeans and corn too," while also cautioning "it's early to speak."
  • (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) signaled continued land trading activity: "we are searching some opportunities" in Brazil where high rates "14, 15 or more" are "pushing some of them to leave the business" and said, "we are expecting a year with the 2 with the sales and buys at the same."

Financial results

  • (CFO Matias Gaivironsky) described key P&L drivers as dominated by valuation and FX/inflation mechanics, noting that in the quarter "the devaluation was 2%, inflation was 6%" and that this "generate a lot of distortions in our balance sheet."
  • (CFO Gaivironsky) said agriculture operating results showed "a significant improvement from last year to this quarter" with "the main difference" being "farmland sales" including Rio do Meio, and added that "BrasilAgro posted gains" on receivables indexed to soybean bags due to a "positive evolution on prices."
  • (CFO Gaivironsky) said profitability headwinds appeared in cattle: "we see a negative evolution" that was "basically in the line of cattle" as inflation-adjusted accounting led to losses when revaluing stock.
  • (CFO Gaivironsky) detailed financial lines: last year there was "a loss of ARS 18.1 billion" in net FX result, while "this year, we posted a gain of ARS 57.6 billion" and said, "we finished the quarter with a gain of ARS 26.3 billion" ("positive compared last year with ARS 146.8 billion").
  • (CFO Gaivironsky) said "the net debt remained stable" versus the end of June, and added: "After the dividend, we will see a decrease to $313 million with a debt amortization schedule that is manageable for the next years."

Q&A

  • Santiago Donato (Investor Relations Officer): If the current dividend payout is sustainable? (Chief Financial & Administrative Officer Gaivironsky): "we don't have a fixed dividend policy" and Cresud decides annually based on "the liquidity position, the debt position, the CapEx that the company needs," adding, "we don't want to be attached to a dividend policy since Argentina has sometimes volatility."
  • Santiago Donato (Investor Relations Officer): Are you seeing opportunities to buy land in Argentina or the region? (Second Vice Chairman, CEO, & GM Elsztain): "we are searching some opportunities" mainly in Brazil because "some are forced to sell" given "interest rate of 14, 15 or more"; in Argentina, "the debt is not at all relevant," and he added, "we are expecting some new sales for the year too."
  • Santiago Donato (Investor Relations Officer): How does the company think about IRSA long term, and will it keep distributing IRSA shares via dividends? (CEO Alejandro Elsztain): "We are not going to sell IRSA" and said the stake remains strategic for counter-cyclical exposure, adding, "We distribute 2%, but still we have 53% of the shares."

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts were not identified in the transcript; questions were routed through the Investor Relations Officer, and the tone centered on dividends, land deals, and portfolio strategy without confrontational follow-ups.
  • Management tone was positive on operations and weather: (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) said, "we are expecting a very good year" and "being very optimistic on the next 3 quarters," while using cautionary qualifiers on crop profitability ("it's early to speak") and cattle ("a little lower margins comparing to last year").
  • A quarter-over-quarter sentiment comparison was not possible because the prior-quarter transcript was not provided beyond a note stating it was unavailable.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The previous-quarter transcript was not available in the prompt, so changes in guidance language, metric deltas, and shifts in analyst focus versus last quarter could not be directly compared.

Risks and concerns

  • (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) highlighted weather dispersion risk in Brazil: "uneven rainfall distribution during Niño" and "the drought could be coming to northern parts" including "Western Bahia and Mapito regions" where Cresud has exposure.
  • (CEO Alejandro Elsztain) flagged profitability pressure in cattle: "prices not rebounding" and "we are expecting a little lower margins comparing to last year."
  • (CFO Matias Gaivironsky) emphasized reporting volatility from macro dynamics: "the devaluation was 2%, inflation was 6%" and said this "generate a lot of distortions" in results presentation.

Final takeaway

Management positioned Q1 as the start of a stronger agricultural year, citing a 3% planted-area increase and favorable El Niño moisture for Argentina’s Humid Pampas, while acknowledging potential drought risk in northern Brazil and lower cattle margins due to weak pricing. Alongside farmland monetization in Brazil and a high cash-and-shares dividend tied to IRSA, executives reiterated that IRSA remains a core holding and highlighted FyO’s scale (8.3 million tons) and a move to control Agrofy as part of a broader services and digital ecosystem push.

data.title: High Roller expects prediction markets to drive 2027 growth while outlining 24-month Crypto.com exclusivity
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: High Roller Technologies, Inc. (ROLR) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "On October 21, just over a month after we launched our invitation-only beta, our prediction market brand, ROLR, went live to the general public" (Chief Executive Officer Seth Young), and "eligible customers across the United States can now open an account on our real money prediction markets platform and trade on the events that they care about" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • "High Roller has entered its next chapter, and we expect prediction markets to be the major growth driver for us in 2027" (Chief Executive Officer Young), while emphasizing the near-term focus: "For the rest of 2026, the job is to bring customers onto the platform, learn from every trade, keep improving the product and put our distribution partners to work" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • "It was quickly followed by the launch of our ROLR app in the App Store on November 9" (Chief Executive Officer Young) and "directionally, we expect to launch our Android app via the Google Play Store before the end of this year, subject to App Store approval" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • "We have a very powerful new product release planned before the end of the month" (Chief Executive Officer Young) and "it's public record that we've successfully registered with the NFA as a commodity trading adviser in advance of this particular product release" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • "Flip Pidot joined as our Chief Business Officer in October" and "we also brought on Ben Sutherland as our Senior Vice President of Product and Platform" (Chief Executive Officer Young), alongside a strategy shift in legacy geographies: "we will cease operations in that market" (New Zealand) "as of the effective date" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • "Third quarter net revenues were $2.4 million" and "total operating expenses were $5.1 million" (Chief Financial Officer Adam Felman), with prediction markets economics framed as: "ROLR earns revenue as our customers trade, so revenue grows for trading activity" (Chief Financial Officer Felman).

Outlook

  • "Q3 is the last quarter where prediction markets show up only on the expense side of the ledger" (Chief Executive Officer Seth Young), and "the fourth quarter will be the first to include prediction markets revenue" (Chief Financial Officer Adam Felman).
  • "We expect online casino revenue to step down further from December with a full effect from the first quarter of 2027" (Chief Financial Officer Felman), tied to the New Zealand exit that management said becomes effective December 1.
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s pre-launch posture, management’s language shifted from "we remain on track for that timing" (Chief Executive Officer Young, Q2) to post-launch execution, including "we're ramping" marketing and partnerships and "we'll continue investing in what's working" (Chief Executive Officer Young, Q3).

Financial Results

  • The analysts estimates JSON used numeric fiscal_quarter values rather than Q1–Q4 labels; as provided, it was treated as invalid for estimates comparisons.
  • "Third quarter net revenues were $2.4 million compared with $4.9 million in the third quarter of 2025" (Chief Financial Officer Adam Felman), and "loss from operations was $2.7 million compared with $0.7 million" (Chief Financial Officer Felman).
  • "Net loss from continuing operations was $2.8 million or $0.25 per basic and diluted share" (Chief Financial Officer Felman), and management highlighted comparability: "The prior year quarter included a one-off $3.6 million income tax benefit" (Chief Financial Officer Felman).
  • Liquidity and runway were emphasized: "At September 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents, excluding restricted cash, were $13.4 million" and "we have no outstanding borrowings" (Chief Financial Officer Felman), adding "we believe our existing cash and cash equivalents are sufficient to fund our operations and meet our obligations for at least the next 12 months" (Chief Financial Officer Felman).

Q&A

  • Brian Kinstlinger, Alliance Global Partners: asked whether early customer acquisition cost and marketing lessons were within expectations and whether competitors were intensifying promotions; Chief Executive Officer Seth Young responded, "it's a little too early to dig into the metrics and give you any specific insights" and added, "we're more focused on what we're putting out as our value proposition than what our competitors are at this time."
  • Brian Kinstlinger, Alliance Global Partners: pressed on state-by-state strategy amid legal uncertainty; Chief Executive Officer Young answered, "we have a great marketing plan targeted to states that really fit our target demographic" and said it was built with "a hope for the best plan for the worst scenario."
  • Brian Kinstlinger, Alliance Global Partners: asked how aggressive the out-of-the-gate spend would be; Chief Executive Officer Young said, "we're definitely in growth mode" and "we'll continue investing in what's working. We'll cut what isn't."
  • Brian Kinstlinger, Alliance Global Partners: asked about Crypto.com contract duration and flexibility alongside an FCM evaluation; Chief Executive Officer Young said exclusivity as a guaranteed introducing broker is "exclusive to Crypto.com for a period of 24 months" and added that if the company pursued FCM licensure, "it does not fall under the exclusivity provision of that contract."
  • Carlo Corzine, Dawson James Securities: asked whether cash had been spent with certain marketing partners and requested interim milestones (customers, dollars bet); Chief Executive Officer Young said the marketing allocation was "not something that we've disclosed publicly" and on milestones added, "when the time comes and when the time is right, we'll consider what we release and when," while noting, "we do hope to have some idea of what our unit economics look like" when reporting the first quarter including prediction markets revenue.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was slightly negative to pressing on disclosure and execution risk, including requests for CAC, promotions intensity, state litigation impact, marketing spend transparency, and near-term operating milestones.
  • Management tone was slightly positive but guarded on near-term metrics, using deflection language such as "it's a little too early" (Chief Executive Officer Seth Young) while expressing confidence statements including "we're confident in our playbook" and "we're definitely playing to win" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • Versus Q2, management messaging shifted from launch preparation and timelines to post-launch growth execution, while analyst questioning shifted from pre-launch engagement (free-to-trade challenge) to early unit economics, promotional intensity, and licensing/partner flexibility.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Q3 introduced the central operational inflection that "ROLR went live to the general public" (Chief Executive Officer Seth Young), while Q2 described a pre-launch state where the company "remain[ed] on track" for a target launch date (Chief Executive Officer Young, Q2).
  • Q3 added strategic structure around licensing optionality and partner flexibility, including forming "a new subsidiary called ROLR FCM LLC" (Chief Executive Officer Young) and clarifying that potential FCM operations "would not fall under this exclusivity arrangement with Crypto.com" (Chief Executive Officer Young); Q2 focused more on achieving NFA status and integrating with Crypto.com.
  • Financially, Q3 reported "third quarter net revenues were $2.4 million" (Chief Financial Officer Adam Felman) versus Q2 reporting "net revenues were $2.8 million" for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Chief Financial Officer Felman, Q2), with Q3 explicitly flagging an additional casino revenue step-down expected from December (Chief Financial Officer Felman).

Risks and Concerns

  • "It's a very competitive space" (Chief Executive Officer Seth Young) was management’s framing of market risk, alongside a stated intent to manage efficiency: channels are judged on "conversion, customer quality, retention and revenue relative to cost" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • Regulatory and licensing uncertainty was explicitly caveated: "we cannot assure the timing or outcome of any registration process" (Chief Executive Officer Young) regarding a potential FCM application, while management positioned optionality around "other potential opportunities like the DCM and DCO licenses" (Chief Executive Officer Young).
  • Legacy business contraction risk was reiterated via planned market exits, including "we will cease operations" in New Zealand effective December 1 (Chief Executive Officer Young), and management stated it expected casino revenue to "step down further" from December (Chief Financial Officer Adam Felman).

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as the final quarter before prediction markets contribute revenue, positioning the October 21 public launch and November 9 iOS app release as the operational pivot into 2027, which the CEO said the company expects to be driven primarily by prediction markets. The CFO underscored reduced casino revenue alongside increased launch investment, highlighted cash of $13.4 million with no borrowings and at least 12 months of runway under the current plan, and stated Q4 would be the first quarter to include prediction markets revenue, while Q&A centered on early customer acquisition economics, competitive promotional intensity, and licensing/partner flexibility under a 24-month Crypto.com exclusivity for the guaranteed introducing broker arrangement.

data.title: ESS Tech ceases operations, files for Chapter 7 bankruptcy
data.description:
ESS Tech (GWHT) disclosed Friday it filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy and ceased operations after considering all strategic alternatives.

The company's products had included sodium-ion batteries, which it said "provide a safer, more robust, and sustainable alternative to lithium-ion technology for short- and medium-duration energy storage" and reduce reliance on constrained critical minerals.

ESS Tech (GWHT) shares have traded over the counter after the stock was delisted from the NYSE early last month, and the stock closed at $0.07 on Friday.

data.title: OptimumBank outlines $48M-$50M annual pretax pre-provision run rate as it targets 2027 HUD license
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: OptimumBank Holdings, Inc. (OPHC) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We reported record quarterly net income of approximately $7.2 million" and "net interest income increased to $16.8 million" with "our net interest margin expanded to 4.63%" (CEO Moishe Gubin).
  • "Our balance sheet also continued expanding with total assets reaching approximately $1.6 billion" and "our Tier 1 leverage ratio increasing to 12.23%" (CEO Gubin).
  • "We have been taking a close look at our operations, identifying opportunities to streamline processes, improving productivity and limiting expenses" and "we've already identified efficiencies that we expect to begin realizing over the next several quarters" (CEO Gubin).
  • "Total interest income increased to $25.11 million compared with $21.72 million in the second quarter" and "total interest expense increased to $8.33 million from $7.03 million" (CFO Elliot Nunez).
  • "We recorded a credit loss expense of $1.07 million during the quarter compared with a $37,000 reversal in the second quarter" and "noninterest expense increased to $9 million from $8.38 million" (CFO Nunez).
  • "Optimum Funding is pursuing a new HUD license, which we anticipate receiving in 2027" and Optimum Finance "continued growing its portfolio during the quarter and is becoming a contributor to our earnings" (Managing Director of Investor and Corporate Relations Seth Denison).

Outlook

  • "Our run rate should be easily probably $10 million a quarter, and that should actually probably grow maybe $12 million a quarter" for pretax pre-provision earnings, and "we should be looking at pretax pre-provision $48 million on the year, $50 million on the year" (CEO Gubin).
  • "We found some expenses that we're able to curb, which should probably add between $600 to $600,000 to $2 million a year right to the bottom line" (CEO Gubin).
  • "We anticipate realizing these improvements while maintaining our strong momentum in lending, deposit growth and the continued expansion of our specialty finance businesses" (CEO Gubin).
  • Versus the prior quarter’s EPS framing, management shifted from "increase our forward-looking annual earnings estimate to a range of approximately $1 per share to approximately $1.15 per share" (CEO Moishe Gubin, Q2) to focusing on pretax pre-provision run rate ranges in Q3.

Financial Results

  • "Net income of $7.17 million compared with $6.66 million in the second quarter" and "earnings per share were $0.30 on both basic and diluted basis" (CFO Nunez).
  • "Gross loans increased to $1.37 billion at September 30, 2026" and "total deposits increased to $1.34 billion at September 30, 2026" (CFO Nunez).
  • "Credit quality remained strong" with "nonperforming assets represented 0.11% of total assets" and "net charge-offs to average loans remain at 0%" (CFO Nunez).
  • "In August, OptimumBank Holdings successfully completed a $35 million subordinated debt offer, of which $31 million was contributed directly to the bank as additional capital" (CFO Nunez).
  • "Since September 30, we have successfully completed several private placement transactions... raising an additional $25.4 million of fresh capital" (CEO Gubin).

Q&A

  • Gaurav Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: asked about earnings run rate into 2027; CEO Gubin: "Our run rate should be easily probably $10 million a quarter... maybe $12 million a quarter" and "we should be looking at pretax pre-provision $48 million on the year, $50 million on the year."
  • Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: pressed on expense control; CEO Gubin: "we already found a bunch of things that we are quickly improving and eliminating use of consultants" and "we're looking at every single thing all the way down to the purchasing paper clips."
  • Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: asked about health care lending demand; CEO Gubin: "our pipeline today collectively is like $700 million" and "we're averaging between $50 million and $100 million a month in loan closings" plus "we already closed $41 million of loans" and "we have $80 million approved loans that should close in the next quarter."
  • Mehta, Alliance Global Partners: asked about common dividends; CEO Gubin: "that still remains a subject of debate at the Board level" and "in the meantime, it doesn't make sense yet."
  • Kenneth Billingsley, Compass Point: clarified Optimum Finance vs. Optimum Funding metrics; CEO Gubin: "That was Optimum Funding" and "finance is doing fantastic. It's cash flowing. It's profitable."
  • Billingsley, Compass Point: asked about Optimum Finance funding costs and yields; CEO Gubin: "it's going to be basically SOFR -- I don't remember, SOFR 275, SOFR 250" and "the yield on that is averaging somewhere like a 19% return."
  • Billingsley, Compass Point: asked about variable-rate exposure and higher rates; CEO Gubin: "I don't see a slowdown for us at all" and later added "our loans... are all fixed loans" with repricing mechanics; CFO Nunez: "we have a robust process in place" and "they will have sufficient cash flows to go variable at that point."
  • E-mailed question (Chris Marinac, Brean) on reserves; CFO Nunez: "we do have a 20-year look back" and "I do expect that to grow as we go" with Optimum Finance also "an additive" to allowance.
  • E-mailed question on 2027 loan/deposit growth and expenses; CEO Gubin: "we're going to budget probably for something like $500 million to $600 million of lending" and "overall growth of operating expenses, you're probably talking about also about maybe $1 million."
  • E-mailed question on capital raises; CEO Gubin: "Most likely, it will be somewhere $50 million raise at some point" in 2027 and explained the Q4 private placement process.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly positive and growth-oriented, with repeated probing on run-rate sustainability, expense discipline, and funding mechanics (e.g., "comment on the run rate going forward?" and "provide some color on where you're looking to reduce expenses?") (Gaurav Mehta, Alliance Global Partners).
  • Management tone was positive and confident in growth and demand ("I don't see a slowdown for us at all") while also operationally intense on costs ("we're looking at every single thing") (CEO Gubin).
  • Versus the previous quarter, management’s messaging leaned less on EPS-range guidance and more on operating run-rate and cost takeout timing, while analysts continued to concentrate on Optimum Finance/Funding mechanics and balance sheet growth.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Q3 emphasized operating leverage and expense actions ("eliminating use of consultants") (CEO Gubin), while Q2 highlighted leadership transition and capital structure simplification ("exchange of all outstanding Series B and Series C convertible preferred stock") (Managing Director Denison, Q2).
  • Guidance language shifted from Q2’s EPS framework ("annual earnings estimate... $1... to... $1.15") (CEO Gubin, Q2) to Q3’s pretax pre-provision framework ("$48 million... $50 million") (CEO Gubin).
  • Capital discussion intensified in Q3 with incremental funding sources: Q3 cited the subordinated debt raise and post-quarter private placements ("raising an additional $25.4 million") (CEO Gubin) versus Q2 discussion that referenced ATM usage and broader liquidity goals.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Total interest expense increased... reflecting higher deposit balances, borrowing costs and interest on our recently issued subordinated debt" (CFO Nunez).
  • "Noninterest expense increased... reflecting continued investment in personnel, technology and infrastructure" and management indicated efficiency efforts would take time ("another couple of quarters will clean up what the normal run rate is") (CEO Gubin).
  • Management tied dividend uncertainty to growth capital needs ("there's always going to be a shortfall") and indicated ongoing equity raises are likely ("in '27, we will raise money by hook or by crook") (CEO Gubin).

Final Takeaway

Management presented Q3 as a record quarter with higher net income, an expanded net interest margin, strong credit metrics, and a higher capital base supported by subordinated debt and post-quarter private placements. The CEO framed 2027 around sustaining and growing pretax pre-provision earnings toward a $48 million to $50 million annual level, pairing continued loan growth expectations with granular expense scrutiny, while keeping dividends under board-level debate due to the stated need to retain and raise equity to fund balance sheet expansion.

data.title: SunPower sinks to 52-week low after delaying 10-Q filing, sees Q3 revenue below guidance
data.description:
SunPower (SPWR) plunged 24.3% on Friday, touching a multi-year intraday low of $0.13, after disclosing it is delaying its 10-Q filing and expects Q3 revenue to come in below its guidance.

SunPower (SPWR) said it expects to report Q3 revenue of $65.1M, compared with $64.5M in the year-earlier quarter but below its previous guidance for revenue of more than $75M, and a comprehensive loss, net of tax, of $21.5M, compared with a $13.7M net loss in the same period last year.

In July, SunPower (SPWR) said Q2 results were hurt by issues at SunPower Direct and that management changes were expected to help Q3 results.

SunPower (SPWR) said it expects to file its 10-Q within the five-day grace period.

data.title: SpaceX Flight 15 booster diverts to splashdown, missing planned double catch
More gold analysts turning bearish as $4,000 support breaks
data.description:
As gold prices fail to hold above $4,000/oz, a growing number of analysts have noted that short-term momentum points to further price declines as rising bond yields and a stronger dollar continue to weigh on the metal.

Elevated inflation pressures and comments from Federal Reserve officials supporting a potential 50-bp rate hike next month are solidifying the market's hawkish bias, which leaves gold vulnerable to further selling pressure, Commerzbank commodity analyst Carsten Fritsch said in a note.

"Since Tuesday, the price has lost almost 7%, or around $290. Interest rate expectations have not risen that much since then, and bond yields are still below the level of early October," Fritsch wrote. "The risk is that ETF investors may start to sell in view of the price weakness. In this case, a further price decline would be expected."

Gold's recent selloff reflects more than a technical correction, as investors are being forced to reassess inflation risks and the Fed's monetary policy outlook, according to XS.com's Simon-Peter Massabni.

The dollar's rise to its highest level since April 2025 and elevated Treasury yields are creating significant obstacles for gold, Massabni said, and with the 10-year Treasury yield moving back above 5%, the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding precious metal continues to increase.

Gold's inability to hold support at $4K has created some technical chart damage, but investors should not confuse short-term weakness with the metal's long-term fundamentals, Saxo Bank's Head of Commodity Strategy Ole Hansen said in a note.

"Central banks continue accumulating bullion as part of their reserve diversification strategies, while ETF investors have demonstrated resilience despite recent volatility. These underlying sources of demand may help limit the correction but are unlikely to prevent further short-term weakness if yields and the dollar continue rising," Hansen wrote.

Gold futures finished little changed in choppy trading Friday, as a lower-than-expected U.S. producer price reading for October and steadier oil prices eased inflation concerns that weighed on prices in the previous session.

Front-month Comex gold (XAUUSD:CUR) for November delivery rose less than 0.1% to $3,879.70/oz, its second-lowest settlement value this year, and front-month Comex November silver (XAGUSD:CUR) slipped 1.9% to $49.031/oz, its lowest settlement value since November 7 last year.

For the full week, gold and silver fell 4.5% and 5.3%, respectively.
